newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Vivid interest in Belgian fin services sector.
newsitem.headline: Vivid interest in Belgian fin services sector.

text.p: Financial services sectors in Belgium, France and the Netherlands are seeing vivid interest from abroad, mainly when it comes to serving the wholesale sector, Belgium's Banking and Finance Commission (CBF) said.

Since the January 1, 1996 opening-up of the European investment services market, allowing companies licenced in one EU country to operate in the whole of the EU without having to seek formal permission, the CBF had received some 600 so-called notifications of intention, it said.
Companies notify a watchdog in a foreign country when they move onto the watchdog's turf and offer financial services.

"We have had some 600 notifications of EU-member (companies) to be formally allowed to offer financial services," the CBF said, adding its counterparts in France and the Netherlands had had similar numbers of requests.
The CBF said the majority of the notifications came from Anglo-Saxon countries. Some 50 came from non-EU countries, mainly the U.S.
The CBF said it was currently dealing with a request from Prudential-Bache to set up a subsidiary in Belgium.
